title: Low beta and low volatility: do the calmest liquid stocks earn as much as or more than the jumpiest, after costs?
hypothesis: The low-risk effect: a monthly-rebalanced basket of the lowest-beta (or lowest-volatility) fifth of the liquid 250 earns more per month than the highest fifth and than the whole liquid 250, after costs.

data.stocks: gold/teachers/stock_panel.parquet daily closes and the cost column, 2003-2023; universe = liquidity rank 1-250 on the formation day

definitions.beta: 250-session covariance of the stock's daily return with the Nifty's divided by the Nifty's variance (at least 200 sessions), as of the last session of the month
definitions.volatility: standard deviation of the last 60 daily returns (at least 50)
definitions.baskets: equal weight; formed on the last session of each month from the liquid 250 with a beta (or volatility); held through the next month (daily returns averaged across names; one-day moves over 50% dropped)
definitions.costs: at each rebalance: one-sided turnover (share of the basket replaced) x the average round-trip cost column of the names; the whole-universe basket pays its own turnover the same way

statistics.test: monthly net return difference (basket minus comparison); each month is one block, t across months
statistics.periods: development to 2017, validation 2018-2023; nothing from 2024 on, no sealed folder
statistics.verdict: india/registry.record standard rule; 16 blocks per period

bar.note: family 'portfolio' (12 rows) plus these 4; k frozen at 16

not_claimed: No paper rule changes; the volatility and return-per-risk figures per basket are reported alongside, not tested.
